title: Introduce incremental prefill evaluator and quantization compatibility checker
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Customers tuning cost/latency trade-offs repeatedly ask for safe defaults for prefill/batching and quantization. This PR introduces an incremental prefill evaluator that runs lightweight simulations on production-like traces and a quantization compatibility checker that validates model artifacts against runtime KV/prefix semantics before rollout. Motivation: reduce manual trial-and-error, catch regressions from quant profiles, and provide actionable unit-econ signals (tokens per USD, median P95 latency impact) prior to tenant rollout. Summary of changes: - New service: prefill-evaluator: lightweight sampler + workload replayer that can run in CI and in the console as a dry-run. Produces a compact report with cost, latency, and safety flags. - New linter/checker: quant-compat-check: verifies quantized weights + attention kv-cache replay for semantic-preservation and runtime buffer layout compatibility. - Telemetry: econ.prefill.* tags added to export fine-grained cost deltas and KV cache integrity metrics. - CLI: redwoodctl prefill dryrun and redwoodctl quant check commands. - Tests: synthetic workload replayer, end-to-end fixture with small GPT-like model, unit tests for estimator. Rollout plan: feature flagged behind "prefill-eval". Start with internal tenants and 3 beta customers for 2 weeks; collect signals and revert knob if regressions > 2x cost or functional discrepancies > 0.2% on canonical eval sets. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-3492) [x] unit tests added [x] integration harness for replay [x] CLI and docs updated [x] telemetry and dashboards wiring [x] safety gate: quant-compat must pass before canary. Backwards compatibility: no runtime changes required; checker is additive and will only block rollouts when enabled. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: false-positive quant failures for custom fused kernels. Mitigation: fallback whitelist for verified kernels and a diagnostic mode that dumps replay traces. - Risk: evaluator overhead in CI. Mitigation: incremental mode runs on sampled 1% traces and short-circuits if deltas negligible. Related work: follows patterns from the prefill-sampler and prefilling heuristics implemented in recent batchers (see ENG-2911, PR 246420).

discussion: Ethan Nguyen (reviewer): Can the quant-compat tool produce a per-layer delta report? We had hard-to-debug failures with adversarial fused kernels.

Maya Patel (author): Yes — checker now emits per-layer MSE of key/values and a small sample of replayed inputs when delta > threshold. Added kernel-whitelist flag for teams using custom fused kernels.
Sofia Morales (reviewer): The early-exit heuristic looks risky for long-tail traffic. Do we have a guard to avoid skipping evaluation for tenants with bursty patterns?
Maya Patel (author): Added burst-detection: if variance > configured threshold, evaluator increases sampling window and disables early-exit. Default remains conservative for safety.
Ravi Singh (reviewer): CI replay flakes on macOS runners; recommend moving the heavy e2e to Linux-only and create a CI gate.
Maya Patel (author): Adjusted CI matrix and marked e2e as linux-only; added a lightweight linux emulation job for PR feedback.
QA (comment): Recommend adding a synthetic regression test that models a small attention-layout change; added as tests/e2e/prefill_replay_test.go
release_notes: Add incremental prefill evaluator and quantization compatibility checker: CLI dry-run commands, telemetry tags econ.prefill.*, safety gate for quant rollouts, and console docs. No breaking changes. Enables pre-deployment cost/latency forecasts and quant sanity checks.
notes_for_oncall: If any customer reports increased inference errors after a quant rollout, check quant-compat failure logs (service: quant-compat) and replay traces under /var/tmp/prefill-replay for the tenant. The feature starts behind flag 'prefill-eval' — safe to toggle off.
safety_gate: quant-compat must pass for canary; evaluator flags 'cost_regression' and 'semantic_drift' if thresholds exceeded
